global_briefing: Watch US moves to keep AI data-centre construction onshore. If they hold, copper, electrical steel, and grid spending concentrate in North America, and utility tariff fights become the place where AI demand meets political limits. Tighter US chip controls, and reported halts to Nvidia server shipments into Southeast Asia, could slow Asian data-centre build and trim Asian copper demand with a lag. Japan's move to triple its Saudi crude reserves keeps diesel costs a live risk for North American haulage. In West Africa, strain in the Guinea–Burkina gold corridor raises the chance that artisanal output shifts in ways that official tonnes will not capture quickly.
